claim: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is a genetic cardiac disease that leads to ventricular tachycardia (VT).
source: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is a genetic cardiac disease that leads to ventricular tachycardia (VT), a life-threatening heart rhythm disorder.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about ARVC.

claim: Geno-DT accurately predicted VT circuit locations for GE patients with 100% sensitivity, 94% specificity, and 96% accuracy.
source: we found that Geno-DT accurately and non-invasively predicted the VT circuit locations for both genotypes (with 100%, 94%, 96% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for GE patient group, and 86%, 90%, 89% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for PKP2 patient group), when compared to VT circuit locations identified during clinical EP studies.
evidence: The abstract reports specific performance metrics from the study comparing Geno-DT predictions to clinical EP studies.

claim: Geno-DT accurately predicted VT circuit locations for PKP2 patients with 86% sensitivity, 90% specificity, and 89% accuracy.
source: we found that Geno-DT accurately and non-invasively predicted the VT circuit locations for both genotypes (with 100%, 94%, 96% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for GE patient group, and 86%, 90%, 89% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for PKP2 patient group), when compared to VT circuit locations identified during clinical EP studies.
evidence: The abstract reports specific performance metrics from the study comparing Geno-DT predictions to clinical EP studies.

claim: In GE patients, fibrotic remodeling is the primary contributor to VT circuits.
source: We determined that in GE patients, fibrotic remodeling is the primary contributor to VT circuits, while in PKP2 patients, slowed conduction velocity and altered restitution properties of cardiac tissue, in addition to the structural substrate, are directly responsible for the formation of VT circuits.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: In PKP2 patients, slowed conduction velocity and altered restitution properties of cardiac tissue, in addition to the structural substrate, are directly responsible for the formation of VT circuits.
source: We determined that in GE patients, fibrotic remodeling is the primary contributor to VT circuits, while in PKP2 patients, slowed conduction velocity and altered restitution properties of cardiac tissue, in addition to the structural substrate, are directly responsible for the formation of VT circuits.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: ARVC has a prevalence estimated as high as 1 in 1000.
source: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is an inherited cardiac disease that affects young adults and has a prevalence estimated as high as 1 in 1000 (Sen-Chowdhry et al., 2010).
evidence: This prevalence estimate is cited from Sen-Chowdhry et al., 2010.

claim: ARVC accounts for up to 10% of unexplained sudden cardiac death cases in people younger than 65 years old.
source: ARVC is a major cause of ventricular tachycardia (VT), a life-threatening fast heart rhythm that can lead to sudden cardiac death (SCD) and accounts for up to 10% of unexplained SCD cases in people younger than 65 years old (Calkins et al., 2017; Thiene et al., 2007).
evidence: This statistic is cited from Calkins et al., 2017 and Thiene et al., 2007.

claim: The success rate of catheter ablation in ARVC patients is only 50–80%.
source: Catheter ablation, which delivers energy to disrupt abnormal electrical conduction, is a mainstay in treating sustained VT in ARVC, but the success rate of ablation in ARVC patients is only 50–80% (Mathew et al., 2019; Arbelo and Josephson, 2010)
evidence: This success rate is cited from Mathew et al., 2019 and Arbelo and Josephson, 2010.

claim: PKP2 is the most common genotype in ARVC, observed in 60% to 78% of ARVC patients with known pathogenic variants.
source: Among these, PKP2 is the most common genotype, observed in 60% to 78% of ARVC patients with known pathogenic variants (Mahdieh et al., 2018; Protonotarios et al., 2022; Corrado et al., 2020).
evidence: This prevalence is cited from multiple sources: Mahdieh et al., 2018; Protonotarios et al., 2022; Corrado et al., 2020.

claim: Around one-third of all ARVC patients do not have known causal pathogenic variants.
source: Interestingly, around one-third of all ARVC patients do not have known causal pathogenic variants (Protonotarios et al., 2022; Corrado et al., 2020; James et al., 2021).
evidence: This proportion is cited from Protonotarios et al., 2022; Corrado et al., 2020; James et al., 2021.

claim: The pathogenesis of gene-elusive ARVC patients is highly associated with frequent high-intensity exercises that lead to fibrosis formation on the RV.
source: The pathogenesis of these gene-elusive (GE) patients is highly associated with frequent high-intensity exercises that lead to fibrosis formation on the RV (Benito et al., 2011; Breuckmann et al., 2009; Sawant et al., 2014).
evidence: This association is cited from Benito et al., 2011; Breuckmann et al., 2009; Sawant et al., 2014.

claim: The retrospective study included 16 ARVC patients with two genotypes: PKP2 (n=8) and gene-elusive (n=8).
source: In our retrospective study of 16 ARVC patients with two genotypes: plakophilin-2 (PKP2, n = 8) and gene-elusive (GE, n = 8)
evidence: The study design and patient numbers are explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: All 16 patients in the cohort were adults with a median age of 31 years.
source: All patients were adults with a median age of 31 years, and 75% of them were female.
evidence: Patient demographics are reported in the Results section.

claim: 75% of the patients in the cohort were female.
source: All patients were adults with a median age of 31 years, and 75% of them were female.
evidence: Patient demographics are reported in the Results section.

claim: All patients had VTs induced during clinical EPS.
source: All had VTs induced during clinical EPS, where information about the patients' VTs were recorded.
evidence: This is stated as an inclusion criterion for the study cohort.

claim: Eight patients were found to have PKP2 loss-of-function variants.
source: Eight patients were found to have PKP2 loss-of-function variants, while the remaining eight did not test positive for variants in any of the known causal genes and were thus considered gene-elusive (GE; James et al., 2021).
evidence: The genetic testing results for the cohort are reported in the Results section.

claim: All 16 patients had RV enhancement on LGE-CMR.
source: All 16 patients had RV enhancement on LGE-CMR; none of them exhibited enhancement on the left ventricle (LV).
evidence: This imaging finding is reported for the entire cohort.

claim: None of the 16 patients exhibited enhancement on the left ventricle.
source: All 16 patients had RV enhancement on LGE-CMR; none of them exhibited enhancement on the left ventricle (LV).
evidence: This imaging finding is reported for the entire cohort.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in clinical parameters between the GE and PKP2 groups.
source: There was also no statistically significant difference in any of the other common clinical features between the two genotype groups.
evidence: This is stated after comparing various clinical parameters between the two groups.

claim: The PKP2 cell model has a peak inward sodium current of -171.56 pA/pF at a membrane potential of -36 mV.
source: The new PKP2 model includes a downscaled maximum conductance for the sodium current (INa), resulting in a peak inward sodium current at a membrane potential of –36 mV that is truncated from –502.71 pA/pF in the GE model to –171.56 pA/pF in the PKP2 model (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is reported as a result of the PKP2 cell model development and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The GE cell model has a peak inward sodium current of -502.71 pA/pF at a membrane potential of -36 mV.
source: The new PKP2 model includes a downscaled maximum conductance for the sodium current (INa), resulting in a peak inward sodium current at a membrane potential of –36 mV that is truncated from –502.71 pA/pF in the GE model to –171.56 pA/pF in the PKP2 model (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is reported as a comparison to the PKP2 model and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The calcium transient in the PKP2 cell model has a longer time to peak (32 vs 27 ms) compared to the GE model.
source: The CaT in the PKP2 cell model has a longer time to peak (32 vs 27 ms), a significantly higher peak (0.0023 vs 0.00084 mM), and a shorter time to 90% return from peak (319 vs 379 ms).
evidence: This is reported as a characteristic of the PKP2 cell model compared to the GE model.

claim: The calcium transient in the PKP2 cell model has a significantly higher peak (0.0023 vs 0.00084 mM) compared to the GE model.
source: The CaT in the PKP2 cell model has a longer time to peak (32 vs 27 ms), a significantly higher peak (0.0023 vs 0.00084 mM), and a shorter time to 90% return from peak (319 vs 379 ms).
evidence: This is reported as a characteristic of the PKP2 cell model compared to the GE model.

claim: The calcium transient in the PKP2 cell model has a shorter time to 90% return from peak (319 vs 379 ms) compared to the GE model.
source: The CaT in the PKP2 cell model has a longer time to peak (32 vs 27 ms), a significantly higher peak (0.0023 vs 0.00084 mM), and a shorter time to 90% return from peak (319 vs 379 ms).
evidence: This is reported as a characteristic of the PKP2 cell model compared to the GE model.

claim: The downregulation of INa in the PKP2 cell model results in a lower upstroke peak and slower maximum upstroke velocity.
source: The downregulation of INa results in a lower upstroke peak and slower maximum upstroke velocity (Vmax).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the INa modification in the PKP2 model.

claim: The PKP2 cell model exhibits an elevated resting membrane potential compared to the GE model.
source: The changes to calcium handling led to an elevated resting membrane potential and longer AP duration at 90% depolarization (APD90).
evidence: This is stated as a result of calcium handling modifications in the PKP2 model.

claim: The PKP2 cell model exhibits a longer AP duration at 90% depolarization (APD90) compared to the GE model.
source: The changes to calcium handling led to an elevated resting membrane potential and longer AP duration at 90% depolarization (APD90).
evidence: This is stated as a result of calcium handling modifications in the PKP2 model.

claim: The maximum slope of the restitution curve was 1.16 for the GE cell model.
source: The maximum slopes of the restitution curves were measured to be 1.16 and 0.59 for the GE and PKP2 cell models, respectively.
evidence: This measurement is reported from the restitution curve analysis.

claim: The maximum slope of the restitution curve was 0.59 for the PKP2 cell model.
source: The maximum slopes of the restitution curves were measured to be 1.16 and 0.59 for the GE and PKP2 cell models, respectively.
evidence: This measurement is reported from the restitution curve analysis.

claim: Across the entire ARVC cohort, diffuse fibrosis was most abundant at the base of the RV and least abundant at the RV apex.
source: We found that across the entire ARVC cohort, the diffuse fibrosis was most abundant at the base of the RV and least abundant at the RV apex (Figure 4A).
evidence: This finding is reported from analysis of the LGE-reconstructed ventricular models and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: There were significant differences in the amount of diffuse fibrosis between the basal (14.01 ± 4.37%), mid (5.41 ± 2.61%), and apical (1.13 ± 1.71%) regions of the RV (p < 0.0001 for pairwise comparisons).
source: There were significant differences in the amount of diffuse fibrosis between the basal, mid, and apical regions (14.01 ± 4.37% for basal RV vs 5.41 ± 2.61% for mid RV vs 1.13 ± 1.71% for apical RV, p < 0.0001 for pairwise comparisons).
evidence: This statistical comparison is reported from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: There were significant differences in dense scar amounts between the basal (5.51 ± 2.71%), mid (1.74 ± 1.99%), and apical (0.42 ± 0.90%) regions of the RV (p < 0.05 for pairwise comparisons).
source: A similar trend was observed for dense scar amounts with significant differences between the basal, mid, and apical regions (5.51 ± 2.71% vs 1.74 ± 1.99% vs 0.42 ± 0.90%, p < 0.05 for pairwise comparisons; Figure 4B).
evidence: This statistical comparison is reported from the structural remodeling analysis and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was no significant difference in the amounts of structural remodeling between anterior, lateral, and posterior regions of the RV.
source: There was no significant difference when comparing the amounts of structural remodeling between anterior, lateral, and posterior regions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: GE patients had a significantly higher amount of diffuse fibrosis than PKP2 patients in the basal anterior wall (6.07 ± 3.18% vs 1.85 ± 0.017%, p < 0.01).
source: We found that the distribution of diffuse fibrosis was different in the two patient groups, with GE patients having a significantly higher amount of diffuse fibrosis burden than PKP2 patients in the basal anterior wall (6.07 ± 3.18% vs 1.85 ± 0.017%, p < 0.01 for pairwise comparisons)
evidence: This comparison between genotype groups is reported from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: GE patients had a significantly higher amount of diffuse fibrosis than PKP2 patients in the basal lateral wall (5.77 ± 2.34% vs 3.24 ± 1.40%, p < 0.05).
source: and basal lateral wall (5.77 ± 2.34% vs 3.24 ± 1.40%, p < 0.05 for pairwise comparisons)
evidence: This comparison between genotype groups is reported from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: GE patients had a significantly lower amount of diffuse fibrosis than PKP2 patients in the basal posterior wall (3.36 ± 2.92% vs 7.73 ± 4.38%, p < 0.05).
source: and a significantly lower amount in the basal posterior wall (3.36 ± 2.92% vs 7.73 ± 4.38%, p < 0.05 for pairwise comparisons; Figure 4C).
evidence: This comparison between genotype groups is reported from the structural remodeling analysis and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There was no statistical significance in the dense scar distribution between the two genotype groups.
source: There was no statistical significance in the dense scar distribution between the two genotype groups.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: A total of 144 ventricular simulations (16 patients × 9 pacing locations) were performed to determine the induced VT circuit morphologies.
source: We performed a total of 144 ventricular simulations (16 patients ✕ 9 pacing locations) to determine the induced VT circuit morphologies.
evidence: This is stated as the number of simulations conducted in the study.

claim: There is a highly positive correlation between the number of VTs induced during EPS and the volume of structural remodeling in the GE patient group (r = 0.91, 0.91, 0.92 for DF, DS and TFV respectively).
source: Our analysis revealed a highly positive correlation between the number of VTs induced during EPS and the volume of each type of structural remodeling (both DF and DS) and total fibrotic volume (TFV) in the GE patient group (r = 0.91, 0.91, 0.92 for DF, DS and TFV respectively)
evidence: This correlation analysis is reported from examining the relationship between structural remodeling and VT inducibility.

claim: There is a moderate correlation between the number of VTs induced during EPS and the volume of structural remodeling in the PKP2 patient group (r = 0.65, 0.7, 0.7 for DF, DS and TFV respectively).
source: while in the PKP2 group, we observed only moderate correlation (r = 0.65, 0.7, 0.7 for DF, DS and TFV respectively).
evidence: This correlation analysis is reported from examining the relationship between structural remodeling and VT inducibility.

claim: There is a strong correlation between VTs induced during EPS and those induced in simulations within the different RV regions in both patient groups (r = 0.99 for both groups).
source: Importantly, we found a strong correlation between VTs induced during EPS and those induced in simulations within the different RV regions in both patient groups (r = 0.99 for both groups)
evidence: This correlation analysis demonstrates the predictive capability of the Geno-DT models.

claim: In the GE patient group, Geno-DT resulted in 28 distinct VTs being induced, 25 of which were observed during EPS.
source: In the GE patient group, Geno-DT resulted in 28 distinct VTs being induced, 25 of which were observed during EPS.
evidence: This is reported as a result of the VT prediction analysis.

claim: In the PKP2 patient group, 25 VT morphologies were induced in PKP2 ARVC models and 25 were reported in the EPS record.
source: The PKP2 group showed comparable results, with 25 VT morphologies induced in PKP2 ARVC models and 25 reported in the EPS record.
evidence: This is reported as a result of the VT prediction analysis.

claim: Geno-DT captured all VT locations observed during EPS in the GE group except for one VT on the mid lateral RV wall.
source: In terms of VT circuit locations, Geno-DT captured all VT locations that were observed during EPS except for one VT on the mid lateral RV wall in the GE group.
evidence: This is reported as a result of comparing predicted VT locations to clinical observations.

claim: In the PKP2 group, Geno-DT predicted all the VT locations recorded during EPS, except for one VT on the basal anterior RV wall and two on the basal posterior wall.
source: In the PKP2 group, Geno-DT predicted all the VT locations recorded during EPS, except for one VT on the basal anterior RV wall and two on the basal posterior wall.
evidence: This is reported as a result of comparing predicted VT locations to clinical observations.

claim: The reduced Vmax in the PKP2 cell model resulted in slower wavefront conduction, particularly in non-fibrotic regions adjacent to the dense fibrosis.
source: Previous study has shown that a decrease in Vmax directly affects the conduction velocity in the cardiac tissue (Issa et al., 2019). Consistent with this relationship, we observed that the reduced Vmax in the PKP2 cell model, caused by downregulated INa, resulted in slower wavefront conduction, particularly in non-fibrotic regions adjacent to the dense fibrosis.
evidence: This observation is reported from the mechanistic analysis and is consistent with cited literature (Issa et al., 2019).

claim: In PKP2 hearts, extended refractoriness and decreased conduction velocity resulted in wavefronts of higher curvature, subsequent source-sink mismatch and conduction block.
source: Hence in PKP2 hearts, extended refractoriness and decreased conduction velocity resulted in wavefronts of higher curvature, subsequent source-sink mismatch and conduction block, setting the stage for arrhythmogenesis.
evidence: This mechanistic explanation is provided based on the study's findings.

claim: The maximum channel conductance for sodium current (INa) was decreased by 70% in the PKP2 ionic model.
source: In our PKP2 ionic model, the maximum channel conductance for sodium current (INa) was decreased by 70% to reflect reported experimental current dynamics from Sato et al., 2009.
evidence: This modification is described in the Materials and methods section and is based on experimental data from Sato et al., 2009.

claim: The maximal conductance of ICaL was scaled by 50% in the PKP2 model.
source: We scaled the maximal conductance of ICaL by 50%, reducing its peak current (9.03 vs 6.84 pA/pF) proportional to the experimental values.
evidence: This modification is described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The background calcium current (IbCa) was upregulated by fivefold in the PKP2 model.
source: To counteract the accompanying decrease in CaT amplitude produced by this modification, we also upregulated the background calcium current (IbCa), representative of connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannel-mediated calcium entry, by fivefold.
evidence: This modification is described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: PKP2-deficient cardiomyocytes have reduced ryanodine receptor (RYR2) channel expression but enhanced channel sensitivity to calcium.
source: Studies from Lyon et al. have further shown that PKP2-deficient cardiomyocytes have reduced ryanodine receptor (RYR2) channel expression but enhanced channel sensitivity to calcium.
evidence: This is cited from studies by Lyon et al.

claim: The sodium-calcium exchanger current (INaCa) was downregulated by 20% in the PKP2 model.
source: a 20% downregulation of the sodium-calcium exchanger current (INaCa) further contributed to this reduced gradient.
evidence: This modification is described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Voxels with intensity ≥4 SD above the reference mean were classified as dense scar region.
source: We used the mean value of the low-intensity region as the reference mean of non-fibrotic myocardium and an intensity of ≥4 SD above the reference mean was classified as the dense scar region.
evidence: This is described as the method for classifying tissue types from LGE-CMR.

claim: Voxels between 2 and 4 SDs above the reference mean were classified as diffuse fibrosis.
source: Voxels between 2 and 4 SDs above the reference mean were classified as diffuse fibrosis; all other voxels were labeled as non-fibrotic myocardium (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is described as the method for classifying tissue types from LGE-CMR, with citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: High-resolution finite-element tetrahedral meshes were generated with an average resolution of 398 μm.
source: After identifying all different tissue types, we generated high-resolution finite-element tetrahedral meshes with an average resolution of 398 μm from the segmentation using finite-element analysis software (Mimics Innovation Suite; Materialise, Leuven, Belgium), as done previously (O'Hara et al., 2022).
evidence: This is described as the method for generating computational meshes.

claim: The study has a small sample size, limited by the fact that ARVC is relatively a rare disease.
source: Our study has a small sample size, limited by the fact that ARVC is relatively a rare disease.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a study limitation.

claim: Most clinical VT ablation sites are on the RV for ARVC, even for those with LV involvement.
source: Additionally, our study focused on patients with only RV enhancement since research has shown that most clinical VT ablation sites are on the RV for ARVC, even for those with LV involvement (Marchlinski et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from Marchlinski et al., 2021 as justification for the study's focus.

claim: The Geno-DT approach integrates patient's disease-induced structural remodeling reconstructed from contrast-enhanced magnetic-resonance imaging and genotype-specific cellular EP properties.
source: This approach integrates the patient's disease-induced structural remodeling reconstructed from contrast-enhanced magnetic-resonance imaging and genotype-specific cellular EP properties.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the Geno-DT approach.

claim: The PKP2 protein plays a significant role in maintaining the structural integrity of the ventricular myocardium and in facilitating signal transduction pathways.
source: The PKP2 protein plays a significant role in maintaining the structural integrity of the ventricular myocardium and in facilitating signal transduction pathways, thus PKP2 pathogenic variants lead to fibrotic remodeling and subsequently to distorted electrical conduction (Vimalanathan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Vimalanathan et al., 2018.

claim: PKP2 pathogenic variants lead to fibrotic remodeling and subsequently to distorted electrical conduction.
source: The PKP2 protein plays a significant role in maintaining the structural integrity of the ventricular myocardium and in facilitating signal transduction pathways, thus PKP2 pathogenic variants lead to fibrotic remodeling and subsequently to distorted electrical conduction (Vimalanathan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Vimalanathan et al., 2018.

claim: Both structural and genotype-modulated electrical abnormalities serve as essential VT substrates in ARVC.
source: Overall, both structural and genotype-modulated electrical abnormalities serve as essential VT substrates in ARVC (El-Battrawy et al., 2018)
evidence: This is cited from El-Battrawy et al., 2018.

claim: There is a high rate of VT recurrence after catheter ablation in ARVC patients.
source: Catheter ablation, which delivers energy to disrupt abnormal electrical conduction, is a mainstay in treating sustained VT in ARVC, but the success rate of ablation in ARVC patients is only 50–80% (Mathew et al., 2019; Arbelo and Josephson, 2010) and there is a high rate of VT recurrence (Waintraub and Gandjbakhch, 2020).
evidence: This is cited from Waintraub and Gandjbakhch, 2020.

claim: VT recurrence can occur as early as a few months after the initial ablation procedure.
source: Difficulty in identifying and targeting all VT circuits could lead to VT recurrence as early as a few months after the initial procedure (Souissi et al., 2018; Mathew et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Souissi et al., 2018 and Mathew et al., 2019.

claim: Most ARVC cases are associated with mutations in desmosomal genes, including plakophilin-2 (PKP2), desmoglein-2 (DSG2), desmocollin-2 (DSC2), plakoglobin (JUP), and desmoplakin (DSP).
source: Most ARVC cases are associated with mutations in desmosomal genes, including plakophilin-2 (PKP2), desmoglein-2 (DSG2), desmocollin-2 (DSC2), plakoglobin (JUP), and desmoplakin (DSP) (Dalal et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from Dalal et al., 2005.

claim: The GE cell model exhibited a decrease in APD90 with diastolic interval (DI) shortening.
source: The GE cell model exhibited a decrease in APD90 with diastolic interval (DI) shortening (Figure 3A), consistent with normal calcium-handling behavior (Franz, 2003).
evidence: This is reported from the restitution analysis and shown in Figure 3A, consistent with cited literature (Franz, 2003).

claim: The PKP2 cell model's AP showed some shortening of phase two duration but with very little reduction in plateau amplitude at fast pacing.
source: In contrast, the PKP2 cell model's AP showed some shortening of phase two duration but with very little reduction in plateau amplitude, resulting in more triangular APs at fast pacing without much change in total duration.
evidence: This is reported from the restitution analysis.

claim: The GE cell APD90 decreased to 148ms before loss-of-capture.
source: While the GE cell APD90 continued to decrease to 148ms before loss-of-capture, the PKP2 cell APD90 only decreased to 208 ms.
evidence: This is reported from the restitution curve analysis.

claim: The PKP2 cell APD90 only decreased to 208 ms before loss-of-capture.
source: While the GE cell APD90 continued to decrease to 148ms before loss-of-capture, the PKP2 cell APD90 only decreased to 208 ms.
evidence: This is reported from the restitution curve analysis.

claim: The substantially lower slope for the PKP2 cell's restitution curve indicated a reduced ability of its AP to adapt to fast pacing rates.
source: The substantially lower slope for the PKP2 cell's restitution curve indicated a reduced ability of its AP to adapt to fast pacing rates.
evidence: This interpretation is provided based on the restitution curve analysis.

claim: Structural remodeling plays a more important role in VT arrhythmogenesis in GE patients than in PKP2 patients.
source: These findings suggest that structural remodeling plays a more important role in VT arrhythmogenesis in GE patients than in PKP2 patients.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the correlation analysis between structural remodeling and VT inducibility.

claim: Additional factors contribute to VT in PKP2 patients, specifically the EP remodeling associated with the PKP2 pathogenic variants.
source: The moderate correlation in the PKP2 group indicates that additional factors contribute to VT, specifically the EP remodeling associated with the PKP2 pathogenic variants.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the correlation analysis showing moderate correlation in PKP2 group.

claim: Geno-DT has the potential to improve pre-ablation planning and to lead to tailored personalized ablation strategies.
source: The Geno-DT approach thus has the potential to improve pre-ablation planning and to lead to tailored personalized ablation strategies.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the Geno-DT approach based on the study's findings.

claim: Geno-DT could save time during the ablation procedure as all possible locations that sustain VTs could be known prior to the procedure.
source: Firstly, it could save time during the ablation procedure as all possible locations that sustain VTs could be known prior to the procedure.
evidence: This is stated as a potential benefit of using Geno-DT in clinical management.

claim: Geno-DT provides a new approach for substrate modification in ARVC ablation, in which the substrate is targeted at predicted VT locations instead of ablating fibrotic tissue or all regions with voltage abnormalities.
source: Secondly, it provides a new approach for substrate modification in ARVC ablation, in which the substrate is targeted at predicted VT locations instead of ablating fibrotic tissue or all regions with voltage abnormalities on electroanatomical mapping, as not all of these are arrhythmogenic (Rottmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a potential benefit of using Geno-DT, with citation to Rottmann et al., 2019.

claim: Not all fibrotic tissue or regions with voltage abnormalities on electroanatomical mapping are arrhythmogenic.
source: Secondly, it provides a new approach for substrate modification in ARVC ablation, in which the substrate is targeted at predicted VT locations instead of ablating fibrotic tissue or all regions with voltage abnormalities on electroanatomical mapping, as not all of these are arrhythmogenic (Rottmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Rottmann et al., 2019.

claim: Excessive ablation lesions have negative consequences on cardiac function, especially in ARVC, as it is characterized by abnormal inflammation response.
source: The latter ablation approaches could lead to excessive lesions, which have negative consequences on cardiac function, especially in ARVC, as it is characterized by abnormal inflammation response (Asatryan et al., 2021; Briceño et al., 2020; Santangeli et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Asatryan et al., 2021; Briceño et al., 2020; Santangeli et al., 2015.

claim: The underlying mechanisms of sustaining VT reentrant circuits differ among various ARVC genotypes.
source: Lastly, our study demonstrated that the underlying mechanisms of sustaining VT reentrant circuits differ among various ARVC genotypes.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Geno-DT could provide a generalized framework to integrate multimodal clinical data and improve precision health for each individual patient.
source: As the understanding of human genetic variation underlying cardiovascular diseases continues to evolve with advances in functional genomics (Li et al., 2022), Geno-DT could provide a generalized framework to integrate multimodal clinical data and improve precision health for each individual patient.
evidence: This is stated as a potential future application of Geno-DT, with citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: Patients were included if they underwent genetic testing for ARVC risk variants that demonstrated either no pathogenic variants (GE patients) or pathogenic PKP2 variant (PKP2 patients).
source: Patients were included if they (1) underwent genetic testing for ARVC risk variants that demonstrated either no pathogenic variants (GE patients) or pathogenic PKP2 variant (PKP2 patients), (2) had inducible VT during EPS, and (3) had LGE-CMR demonstrating the presence of RV fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as an inclusion criterion for the study.

claim: Patients were included if they had inducible VT during EPS.
source: Patients were included if they (1) underwent genetic testing for ARVC risk variants that demonstrated either no pathogenic variants (GE patients) or pathogenic PKP2 variant (PKP2 patients), (2) had inducible VT during EPS, and (3) had LGE-CMR demonstrating the presence of RV fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as an inclusion criterion for the study.

claim: Patients were included if they had LGE-CMR demonstrating the presence of RV fibrosis.
source: Patients were included if they (1) underwent genetic testing for ARVC risk variants that demonstrated either no pathogenic variants (GE patients) or pathogenic PKP2 variant (PKP2 patients), (2) had inducible VT during EPS, and (3) had LGE-CMR demonstrating the presence of RV fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as an inclusion criterion for the study.

claim: For non-fibrotic myocardium regions of the GE group, the ten Tusscher and Panfilov, 2006 model with the addition of a late sodium current representation was used.
source: For non-fibrotic myocardium regions of the GE group, we used the ten Tusscher and Panfilov, 2006 model with the addition of a late sodium current representation (O'Hara et al., 2011).
evidence: This is described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A late sodium current (INaL) formulation was added to the GE model, as done in previous studies.
source: A late sodium current (INaL) formulation was added, as done in our previous studies (Cartoski et al., 2019; Shade et al., 2020; Arevalo et al., 2016; Prakosa et al., 2018; Shade et al., 2021).
evidence: This is described in the Materials and methods section with citations to previous studies.

claim: The PKP2 model was developed by modifying the GE model based on experimental data from Lyon et al., 2021 and Sato et al., 2009.
source: For non-fibrotic myocardium regions of the PKP2 group, we developed a new PKP2 model by modifying the GE model based on experimental data (Lyon et al., 2021 and Sato et al., 2009).
evidence: This is described in the Materials and methods section with citations to experimental data sources.

claim: The PKP2 model recapitulates the altered sodium current dynamics and calcium-handling properties observed in experimental recordings of cardiomyocytes from ARVC hearts.
source: Our resulting PKP2 model recapitulates the altered sodium current dynamics and calcium-handling properties observed in experimental recordings of cardiomyocytes from ARVC hearts.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the developed PKP2 model.

claim: The upregulation of IbCa in the PKP2 model is representative of connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannel-mediated calcium entry.
source: To counteract the accompanying decrease in CaT amplitude produced by this modification, we also upregulated the background calcium current (IbCa), representative of connexin 43 (Cx43) hemichannel-mediated calcium entry, by fivefold.
evidence: This is stated as the biological interpretation of the IbCa modification.

claim: PKP2-deficient cells have disrupted cell-cell adhesion, functional dysregulation of Cx43, increased membrane calcium permeability, and excess free calcium concentrations.
source: This upregulation was in line with the in vitro properties of PKP2-deficient cells: disrupted cell-cell adhesion, functional dysregulation of Cx43, increased membrane calcium permeability, and excess free calcium concentrations.
evidence: This is stated as the in vitro properties of PKP2-deficient cells that justify the model modifications.

claim: The half-saturation constant for sarcoplasmic buffering was reduced by 40% (0.3 vs 0.18 mM) in the PKP2 model to achieve CaSR overload.
source: CaSR overload was achieved by decreasing calsequestrin affinity as a 40% reduction in the half-saturation constant for sarcoplasmic buffering (0.3 vs 0.18 mM).
evidence: This modification is described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The enhanced calcium concentration of all three compartments in the PKP2 model corresponded with the experimentally measured calcium levels for PKP2-deficient cardiomyocytes.
source: The enhanced calcium concentration of all three compartments corresponded with the experimentally measured calcium levels for PKP2-deficient cardiomyocytes and effectively shifted the concentration vs RyR2-binding curve leftward.
evidence: This is stated as validation of the model modifications against experimental data.

claim: For regions of diffuse fibrosis, the TT2 model with modifications based on data reported by Coppini et al., 2013 was used.
source: For regions of diffuse fibrosis, we used the TT2 model with modifications based on data reported by Coppini et al., 2013.
evidence: This is described in the Materials and methods section with citation to Coppini et al., 2013.

claim: The EP properties of the modified model for diffuse fibrosis have been validated in previous studies.
source: The EP properties of this modified model have been validated in previous studies (Shade et al., 2020; O'Hara et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from previous validation studies.

claim: In the diffuse fibrosis model, maximal conductance of INaL and ICaL were respectively increased by 107% and 19%.
source: Maximal conductance of INaL and ICaL were respectively increased by 107% and 19%; maximal conductance of IKr, IKs, Ito, and IK1 were respectively decreased by 34%, 27%, 85%, and 15%; sodium-calcium exchanger activity was upregulated by 34%; sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity was downregulated by 43%.
evidence: These modifications for the diffuse fibrosis model are described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: In the diffuse fibrosis model, maximal conductance of IKr, IKs, Ito, and IK1 were respectively decreased by 34%, 27%, 85%, and 15%.
source: Maximal conductance of INaL and ICaL were respectively increased by 107% and 19%; maximal conductance of IKr, IKs, Ito, and IK1 were respectively decreased by 34%, 27%, 85%, and 15%; sodium-calcium exchanger activity was upregulated by 34%; sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity was downregulated by 43%.
evidence: These modifications for the diffuse fibrosis model are described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: In the diffuse fibrosis model, sodium-calcium exchanger activity was upregulated by 34%.
source: Maximal conductance of INaL and ICaL were respectively increased by 107% and 19%; maximal conductance of IKr, IKs, Ito, and IK1 were respectively decreased by 34%, 27%, 85%, and 15%; sodium-calcium exchanger activity was upregulated by 34%; sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity was downregulated by 43%.
evidence: These modifications for the diffuse fibrosis model are described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: In the diffuse fibrosis model, sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity was downregulated by 43%.
source: Maximal conductance of INaL and ICaL were respectively increased by 107% and 19%; maximal conductance of IKr, IKs, Ito, and IK1 were respectively decreased by 34%, 27%, 85%, and 15%; sodium-calcium exchanger activity was upregulated by 34%; sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase activity was downregulated by 43%.
evidence: These modifications for the diffuse fibrosis model are described in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Each diastolic short-axis image stack had a median of 11 slices with an average of 9.58±2.16 mm slice thickness and average in-plane axial resolution of 1.56±0.49 mm.
source: Each diastolic short-axis image stack had a median of 11 slices with an average of 9.58±2.16 mm slice thickness and average in-plane axial resolution of 1.56±0.49 mm.
evidence: This describes the imaging parameters of the LGE-CMR scans used in the study.

claim: Both the RV and LV myocardium were segmented from the LGE-CMR using a semi-automatic function of CardioViz3D which has been previously validated.
source: Both the RV and LV myocardium were segmented from the LGE-CMR using a semi-automatic function of CardioViz3D which has been previously validated by our team (Arevalo et al., 2016; Shade et al., 2020; Cartoski et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the segmentation method with citations to validation studies.

claim: Otsu thresholding was used to binarize the segmented myocardium into high- and low-intensity regions.
source: We used Otsu thresholding to binarize the segmented myocardium into high- and low-intensity regions.
evidence: This describes the image processing method used.

claim: A validated rule-based method was used to incorporate fiber orientations to each element of the computational mesh.
source: We then used a validated rule-based method to incorporate fiber orientations to each element of the computational mesh (Bayer et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the method for incorporating fiber orientations with citation to Bayer et al., 2012.

claim: The openCARP software package was used to simulate electrical activity in monodomain representation of the myocardium.
source: We used the openCARP software package to simulate electrical activity in monodomain representation of the myocardium (Plank et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the simulation software used with citation to Plank et al., 2021.

claim: Each heart digital twin was paced sequentially from 9 uniformly distributed endocardial RV locations using a validated rapid pacing protocol.
source: Each heart digital twin was paced sequentially from 9 uniformly distributed endocardial RV locations (see Figure 1) using a validated rapid pacing protocol described in our previous studies (Prakosa et al., 2018; Arevalo et al., 2016; Cartoski et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the simulation protocol with reference to Figure 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: At each pacing site, six pacing stimuli (S1) were delivered at a 600ms cycle length, followed by a premature stimulus (S2) delivered 300ms after S1.
source: At each pacing site, six pacing stimuli (S1) were delivered at a 600ms cycle length, followed by a premature stimulus (S2) delivered 300ms after S1.
evidence: This describes the pacing protocol used in the simulations.

claim: Induced VT in the Geno-DT models was defined as re-entry after sustaining at least 2 cycles at the same critical site.
source: Induced VT in the Geno-DT models was defined as re-entry after sustaining at least 2 cycles at the same critical site, as in our previous studies (Sung et al., 2020; Shade et al., 2021).
evidence: This defines the criterion for VT induction with citations to previous studies.

claim: Reentries induced from different pacing sites but occurring in the same location with the same morphology were classified as repetitive.
source: Reentries induced from different pacing sites but occurring in the same location with the same morphology were classified as repetitive.
evidence: This describes the classification method for VT circuits.

claim: Simulations were conducted blind to the clinical data.
source: Simulations were conducted blind to the clinical data.
evidence: This describes the blinding procedure used in the study.

claim: Human experimental data on cellular EP properties for other pathogenic variants implicated in ARVC (e.g., DSP, DSG-2) is lacking.
source: Furthermore, we considered only two genotypes, GE and PKP2, as human experimental data on cellular EP properties for other pathogenic variants implicated in ARVC (e.g., DSP, DSG-2), from which to construct cell models, is lacking
evidence: This is stated as a limitation explaining why only two genotypes were studied.

claim: The prevalence of causal variants other than PKP2 is lower compared to that of PKP2.
source: in addition, because the prevalence of these causal variants is lower compared to that of PKP2, there were not enough patients in the database with the corresponding clinical data needed for model construction and validation (clinical images, EPS study, etc.).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation explaining why only two genotypes were studied.

claim: Previous studies have successfully employed patient-specific heart digital twins in investigating VT mechanisms and in predicting VT locations and morphologies to support ablation targeting in ischemic heart diseases.
source: Previous studies from our group have successfully employed patient-specific heart digital twins in investigating VT mechanisms and in predicting VT locations and morphologies to support ablation targeting in ischemic heart diseases (Prakosa et al., 2018; Deng et al., 2019; Sung et al., 2020; Sung et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies by the research group.

claim: A previous study had incorporated PKP2 cell EP properties in a computational cell model, but the model was too complex to be incorporated into whole-heart simulations.
source: While a previous study had incorporated PKP2 cell EP properties in a computational cell model (Lyon et al., 2021), the model was too complex to be incorporated into whole-heart simulations due to its focus on describing subcellular phenomena.
evidence: This is cited from Lyon et al., 2021 as context for the development of the new PKP2 model.

claim: PKP2 patients with clinical sustained VTs had more fibrotic remodeling in the basal posterior region of RV than the anterior.
source: We found that PKP2 patients with clinical sustained VTs had more fibrotic remodeling in the basal posterior region of RV than the anterior, while the fibrosis distribution in the GE group was consistent with previous findings.
evidence: This is reported as a finding from the structural remodeling analysis.

claim: The fibrosis distribution in the GE group was consistent with previous findings.
source: We found that PKP2 patients with clinical sustained VTs had more fibrotic remodeling in the basal posterior region of RV than the anterior, while the fibrosis distribution in the GE group was consistent with previous findings.
evidence: This is stated as a finding that aligns with prior research.

claim: Different ARVC genotypes exhibit distinct distributions of fibrotic remodeling.
source: These results demonstrate that different ARVC genotypes exhibit distinct distributions of fibrotic remodeling.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comparison of fibrosis distribution between GE and PKP2 groups.

claim: The number of induced VT morphologies was similar between GE and PKP2 patients.
source: Furthermore, while the number of induced VT morphologies was similar between GE and PKP2 patients, our analysis revealed a weaker correlation between the locations of VTs induced during EPS and distribution of fibrosis in the PKP2 group compared to the GE group.
evidence: This is reported as a finding from the VT induction analysis.

claim: Studies of ARVC structural substrates have typically relied on electroanatomical mapping and biopsy, which do not provide a complete characterization of the 3D fibrosis distribution in the right ventricle.
source: Studies of ARVC structural substrates have typically relied on electroanatomical mapping and biopsy, which do not provide a complete characterization of the 3D fibrosis distribution in the right ventricle (Te Riele et al., 2013; Basso et al., 2009; Corrado et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from Te Riele et al., 2013; Basso et al., 2009; Corrado et al., 2005.

claim: The different restitution properties of the PKP2 cell model resulting from the altered calcium handling contributed to the formation of reentry.
source: The different restitution properties of the PKP2 cell model resulting from the altered calcium handling also contributed to the formation of reentry.
evidence: This is stated as a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: The rapid pacing rates used to induce VT corresponded to the steep initial phase of the restitution curves.
source: The rapid pacing rates used to induce VT corresponded to the steep initial phase of the restitution curves, where PKP2 cell model had extended refractoriness compared to the GE cell.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the restitution analysis.

claim: The PKP2 cell model had extended refractoriness compared to the GE cell at rapid pacing rates.
source: The rapid pacing rates used to induce VT corresponded to the steep initial phase of the restitution curves, where PKP2 cell model had extended refractoriness compared to the GE cell.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the restitution analysis.
